ana: Heads-up: found a streaming leak in the python quickstart sample.

ana: Minimal repro:
```py
async def demo():
    it = client.stream_responses("prompt")
    async for frame in it:
        if frame.get('done'):
            break
# process exits but fd stays open until process GC
```

vik: ugh. does `break` not call aclose on that iterator?

ana: looks like the wrapper returned by client.stream_responses() returns a proxy object that doesn't implement `aclose()` forwarding. If the coroutine is cancelled mid-yield the underlying socket isn't closed.

li: can you reproduce in a short script? I can add an integration test.

ana: yes, gist: https://gist.github.com/ana/stream-leak-repro (tiny script with asyncio cancel after first chunk). Repro is deterministic on linux with uvloop and when idle ~20s before cancel.

vik: quick workaround for users: do `async with client.stream_responses(...) as it:` or in try/finally: `await it.aclose()` in finally. That forces socket close.

li: thanks. For onboarding we should update sample to `async with` so new users don't hit fd limits. Also note in docs example that chunks can be bytes or str depending on model/encoding. Typing note: `AsyncIterator[Union[str, bytes, dict]]` is ugly; propose a TypedDict for chunk shape and a top-level alias `Chunk = Union[str, bytes, TokenChunk]`.

vik: good call. I also noticed mypy complains if generator is annotated as `-> AsyncIterator[str]` but yields bytes in tests. We should add a section in docs about the canonical typing and include `# type: ignore[return-value]` examples where necessary.

ana: other idea: provide an `asynccontextmanager` wrapper exported from SDK: `streaming_context(client.stream_responses(...))` that guarantees closure. That is a small DX win without changing runtime semantics.

li: will add an integration test that cancels in mid-frame and asserts fd count drops. I'll add it to sample-apps/streaming-ci and set a CI guard threshold.

vik: I filed an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1589 (py stream iterator aclose missing + typing guidance). Added repro, suggested fixes: forward aclose from proxy, add async context wrapper, update quickstart. @devex-bot label please?

devex-bot: label "streaming" and "py-sdk" added to issue #1589.

ana: small note for maintainers: check client/_stream_wrapper.py and specifically how __aiter__ constructs the proxy. It looks like `types.SimpleNamespace(__anext__=it.__anext__)` which loses `aclose`.

li: also file a follow-up RFC if we want to add an opt-in idle auto-close on iterator objects. Could help serverless customers but might surprise others.

vik: SRE: see INC-2034 which linked an fd spike in staging; likely same pattern. @sre-bot FYI.

sre-bot: incident INC-2034 linked.

ana: I'll open a small PR that updates quickstart, adds the `asynccontextmanager` helper, and includes the cancel test. tagging @li and @vik for review.

vik: thanks! small but important onboarding win. :rocket:
